# Research topics {.unlisted}

[Cortical contributions to gait, quantitative assessment of movement disorders, and methods for reproducible mobile EEG research.]{.dek}
:::

## Mobile EEG during walking {#eeg}

I record EEG during walking and combine it with motion capture, EMG and wearable sensors to study cortical contributions to gait, for example gait-related beta oscillations and corticomuscular coherence, and their changes in Parkinson's disease.

Projects: [StepuP](../projects/stepup.qmd) · [EEGManySteps](../projects/eegmanysteps.qmd) · [Pocketable MoBI](../projects/index.qmd#pocketable) · [EPOC](../projects/index.qmd#epoc)

## Gait and balance {#algorithms}

I develop and validate algorithms that derive gait and balance parameters from wearable and motion-capture data, and apply them in neurological and geriatric cohorts.

Projects: [KielMAT](../software/index.qmd#kielmat) · [StepuP](../projects/stepup.qmd)

## Movement disorders {#datascience}

I use quantitative measures to characterise movement disorders, including the modulation of essential tremor by sensory feedback and arousal, gait measures as progression markers in Parkinson's disease, and the relationship between mobility, cognition and clinical scores in geriatric patients.

Projects: [StepuP](../projects/stepup.qmd) · [Tremor assessment](../projects/index.qmd#tremordetect) · [ComOn](../projects/index.qmd#comon)

## Open and reproducible methods {#open-science}

I study analysis and reporting practices in mobile EEG, contribute to data standards such as Motion-BIDS, and support open-science initiatives in biological psychology.

Projects: [META-REP](../projects/meta-rep.qmd) · [IGOR](../projects/igor.qmd) · [EEGManySteps](../projects/eegmanysteps.qmd) · [Motion-BIDS](../projects/index.qmd#motion-bids)
